5397-dr-jonathan.title: Dr Jonathan
5397-dr-jonathan.creator: Winston Churchill
5397-dr-jonathan.description: A book by Winston Churchill. SCENE: The library of ASHER PINDAR'S house in Foxon Falls, a New England  village of some three thousand souls, over the destinies of which  the Pindars for three generations have presided. It is a large,  dignified room, built early in the nineteenth century, with white  doors and gloss woodwork. At the rear of the stage,--which is the  front of the house,--are three high windows with small, square panes  of glass, and embrasures into which are fitted white inside  shutters.

arxiv-2106-09724.title: GRUMPY: a simple framework for realistic forward-modelling of dwarf galaxies 2020 GRUMPY: a simple framework for realistic forward-modelling of dwarf galaxies – 20
arxiv-2106-09724.creator: Andrey Kravtsov, Viraj Manwadkar
arxiv-2106-09724.description: Abstract We present a simple regulator-type framework designed specifically for modelling formation of dwarf galaxies. Despite its simplicity, when coupled with realistic mass accretion histories of haloes from simulations and reasonable choices for model parameter values, the framework can reproduce a remarkably broad range of observed properties of dwarf galaxies over seven orders of magnitude in stellar mass.

arxiv-2112-04427.title: II. The effect of axisymmetric and spatially varying equilibria and flow on MHD wave modes: Cylindrical geometry 2021 II. The effect of axisymmetric and spatially varying equilibria and flow on MHD wave modes: Cylindrical geometry – 18
arxiv-2112-04427.creator: S. J. Skirvin, V. Fedun, Suzana S. A. Silva, G. Verth
arxiv-2112-04427.description: Abstract Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) waves are routinely observed in the solar atmosphere. These waves are important in the context of solar physics as it is widely believed they can contribute to the energy budget of the solar atmosphere and are a prime candidate to contribute towards coronal heating.

arxiv-2206-05561.title: Gaia Data Release 3: the Solar System survey
arxiv-2206-05561.creator: P. Tanga, T. Pauwels, F. Mignard, K. Muinonen, A. Cellino, P. David, D. Hestroffer, F. Spoto, J. Berthier, J. Guiraud, W. Roux, B. Carry, M. Delbo, A. Dell’Oro, C. arxiv-2206-05561.description: Abstract Context. The third data release by the Gaia mission of the European Space Agency (DR3) is the first release to provide the community with a large sample of observations for more than 150 thousand Solar System objects, including asteroids and natural planetary satellites.

arxiv-2301-05066.title: Branching symplectic monogenics using a Mickelsson–Zhelobenko algebra
arxiv-2301-05066.creator: David Eelbode, Guner Muarem
arxiv-2301-05066.description: Abstract . In this paper we consider (polynomial) solution spaces for the symplectic Dirac operator (with a focus on 1 1 -homogeneous solutions). This space forms an infinite-dimensional representation space for the symplectic Lie algebra 𝔰 ​ 𝔭 ​ ( 2 ​ m ) \mathfrak{sp}(2m) .

arxiv-2307-08074.title: Disco-Bench: A Discourse-Aware Evaluation Benchmark for Language Modelling Issue: 1
arxiv-2307-08074.creator: Longyue Wang, Zefeng Du, Donghuai Liu, Cai Deng, Dian Yu, Haiyun Jiang, Yan Wang, Leyang Cui, Shuming Shi, Zhaopeng Tu
arxiv-2307-08074.description: Abstract Modeling discourse – the linguistic phenomena that go beyond individual sentences, is a fundamental yet challenging aspect of natural language processing (NLP). However, existing evaluation benchmarks primarily focus on the evaluation of inter-sentence properties and overlook critical discourse phenomena that cross sentences.

arxiv-2309-07374.title: Beta quantile regression for Robust estimation of uncertainty in the presence of outliers
arxiv-2309-07374.creator: Haleh Akrami*, Omar Zamzam*, Anand Joshi, Sergul Aydore, Richard Leahy
arxiv-2309-07374.description: Abstract Quantile Regression (QR) can be used to estimate aleatoric uncertainty in deep neural networks and can generate prediction intervals. Quantifying uncertainty is particularly important in critical applications such as clinical diagnosis, where a realistic assessment of uncertainty is essential in determining disease status and planning the appropriate treatment.

arxiv-2311-06688.title: The Effect of Trust and its Antecedents on Robot Acceptance
arxiv-2311-06688.creator: Katrin Fischer, Donggyu Kim, Joo-Wha Hong
arxiv-2311-06688.description: Abstract As social and socially assistive robots are becoming more prevalent in our society, it is beneficial to understand how people form first impressions of them and eventually come to trust and accept them. This paper describes an Amazon Mechanical Turk study ( n = 239 n=239 ) that investigated trust and its antecedents trustworthiness and first impressions.

arxiv-2408-13113.title: Extremal Structures with Embedded Pre-Failure Indicators - Preprint
arxiv-2408-13113.creator: Christoffer Fyllgraf Christensen, Jonas Engqvist, Fengwen Wang, Ole Sigmund, Mathias Wallin
arxiv-2408-13113.description: Abstract Preemptive identification of potential failure under loading of engineering structures is a critical challenge. Our study presents an innovative approach to built-in pre-failure indicators within multiscale structural designs utilizing the design freedom of topology optimization. The indicators are engineered to visibly signal load conditions approaching the global critical buckling load.

arxiv-2503-20207.title: Reasoning and Learning a Perceptual Metric for Self-Training of Reflective Objects in Bin-Picking with a Low-cost Camera
arxiv-2503-20207.creator: Peiyuan Ni, Chee Meng Chew, Marcelo H. Ang Jr, Gregory S. Chirikjian
arxiv-2503-20207.description: Abstract Bin-picking of metal objects based on low-cost RGBD cameras may suffer errors due to sparse depth information and reflective part texture, leading to a need for manual labeling. To reduce the need for human intervention, we propose a framework consisting of a metric learning stage and a self-training stage.

arxiv-2504-09898.title: The Milky Way Project MOBStIRS: Parametrizing Infrared Stellar-Wind Bow Shock Morphologies with Citizen Science Facilities: Spitzer
arxiv-2504-09898.creator: Angelica S. Whisnant, Matthew S. Povich, Nikhil Patten, Henry A. Kobulnicky
arxiv-2504-09898.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Angelica S. Whisnant, Matthew S. Povich, Nikhil Patten, Henry A. Kobulnicky. Mass-loss influences stellar evolution, especially for massive stars with strong winds. Stellar wind bow shock nebulae driven by Galactic OB stars can be used to measure mass-loss rates ( M ˙ \dot{M} ). The standoff distance ( R 0 R_{0} ) between the star and the bow shock is set by momentum flux balance between the stellar wind and the surrounding interstellar medium (ISM).

arxiv-2505-21941.title: Test-Time Scaling with Repeated Sampling Improves Multilingual Text Generation
arxiv-2505-21941.creator: Ashim Gupta Vivek Srikumar Kahlert School of Computing University of Utah ashim@cs.utah.edu
arxiv-2505-21941.description: Abstract Inference-time scaling via repeated sampling has shown promise in reasoning tasks, but its effectiveness in multilingual generation remains underexplored. We evaluate this approach using perplexity- and reward-based verifiers on two multilingual benchmarks: the Aya Evaluation Suite and m-ArenaHard. Our results show consistent quality improvements, with gains exceeding 35% in some cases.

arxiv-2511-05254.title: A Gate-Based Quantum Genetic Algorithm for Real-Valued Global Optimization
arxiv-2511-05254.creator: Leandro C. Souza, Laurent E. Dardenne, Renato Portugal
arxiv-2511-05254.description: Abstract We propose a gate-based Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA) for real-valued global optimization. In this model, individuals are represented by quantum circuits whose measurement outcomes are decoded into real-valued vectors through binary discretization. Evolutionary operators act directly on circuit structures, allowing mutation and crossover to explore the space of gate-based encodings.

pmc-10646197.title: The impact of nursing practice environments on patient safety culture in primary health care: a scoping review protocol
pmc-10646197.creator: Soraia Cristina de Abreu Pereira, Olga Maria Pimenta Lopes Ribeiro, Cintia Silva Fassarella, Eduardo José Ferreira Santos
pmc-10646197.description: BackgroundPatient safety is a key priority for healthcare organisations. It impacts directly on patient health and wellbeing. The increasing complexity of current healthcare settings, which are associated with high work demands and increasingly stressful professional practice environments, contributes to an increased likelihood of errors and adverse events.

pmc-12506279.title: Exploring the associations of career transition components with adolescents’ career decision-making self-efficacy and anxiety
pmc-12506279.creator: Osman Söner, Olcay Yılmaz
pmc-12506279.description: BackgroundThe transition from high school to college is crucial for adolescents' identity, responsibilities, and career choices and may shape adolescents' lives. This study aims to explore the mediating role of career transition components—situation, self, and support—on the relationship between career decision-making self-efficacy and career anxiety among adolescents.

pmc-12892206.title: The clinical and chest radiographic features of respiratory syncytial virus-associated severe respiratory illness in hospitalised adults in South Africa, 2022 - 2023
pmc-12892206.creator: N Goolam, J Naude, K Bishop, M Zunza, E Irusen, J Moyes, C Cohen, S Walaza, A Parker
pmc-12892206.description: Background In most healthy adults, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes mild self-limiting respiratory infection. However, vulnerable populations may present differently or have more complicated courses of disease. Objectives To describe the clinical and radiographic features of adults hospitalised with RSV-associated severe respiratory illness (SRI) in two urban hospitals during 2022 and 2023.

pmc-13519641.title: A dual-ion/immune checkpoint nanoplatform-activated pyroptosis/cGAS-STING signaling transform iMWA into systemic immunotherapy against HCC recurrence
pmc-13519641.creator: Mengqi Zhang, Chao Rong, Hejia Qin, Xiali Qin, Zelong Jiang, Guanhua Qiu, Tian Qin, Guchun Qin, Niqiang Zhou, Weizhong Tang, Danke Su, Yunxi Huang, Chang Zhao
pmc-13519641.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Incomplete microwave ablation (iMWA) remains a major challenge in the clinical management of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), as residual tumors often foster an immunosuppressive microenvironment and upregulate PD-L1 expression, thereby promoting immune evasion and recurrence. This study systematically elucidates the mechanisms underlying HCC progression and metastasis following iMWA and describes the design of a dual-ion/immune checkpoint nanoplatform (aP@Mn/Ca) based on a metal-organic framework (MOF).
